From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo: model recommendations + prompt/edge-case collection (redaction guidance requested)

Hi Jane / Marco —

Thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can move toward a short pilot: 

Recap (30-min demo)
- Customer goals: 1) improve search relevance for navigational queries, 2) robust entity redaction for PII in user queries, 3) reproducible prompt-driven reranking for results.
- Current infra: on-prem Elasticsearch + API layer; average query length 6–18 tokens; 95th percentile latency requirement 150ms.
- Success metrics: NDCG@10 + human QA pass-rate >= 90% for sampled promoted queries.

Redwood model recommendations (initial shortlist)
- redwood-titan-7b-quant (recommended starting point for balanced latency/cost)
- redwood-gnn-3b-precise (for reranking-heavy flows where precision matters)
- small fallback: redwood-alpine-1.3b (for low-latency fallbacks in Dedicated)

What we need from you (asks) — can you provide by EOD Friday, Nov 6?
1) Prompt set: 200–500 real customer queries, split into: production-facing prompts (what users type) and system-level prompts (pipe/context used by the search service). Use the attached CSV template (acme_prompt_samples_template.csv).
2) Edge-case examples: 20–50 queries that currently degrade quality (examples of hallucinations, toxic content, PII-heavy queries). Mark PII instances where possible.
3) Redaction constraints: any regulatory or legal redaction rules (e.g., keep contact identifiers, mask everything, or country-specific rules). If you prefer, send a short doc and we’ll map to our redaction schema.
4) Benchmarks: if you have recent NDCG runs or offline evaluation spreadsheets, attach them or point us to the secure Drive link.

We attached: redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf (our standard template), acme_prompt_samples_template.csv, and rdw_model-benchmarks-3links.txt (links to three internal benchmark runs for context).

Next steps / timeline
- Friday, Nov 6: Acme shares prompt set + edge-case list + redaction constraints.
- Week of Nov 9: Redwood runs an initial fit check (small eval) + provides quantitative model recommendations and a suggested canary plan for Dedicated.
- Nov 16: pilot kickoff (if fit looks good).

Quick ask: please confirm whether the prompt set can include anonymized user IDs or if you need us to accept only fully redacted text samples.

Thanks — look forward to the files.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf (pdf), acme_prompt_samples_template.csv (csv), rdw_model-benchmarks-3links.txt (txt)

Hi Monica —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications:
- We can share anonymized prompts but might need to scrub account numbers; we will flag PII in a "pii_flag" column in the CSV.
- Edge-case set: Marco will compile the initial list; targeting 30 examples.
- On redaction rules: we follow GDPR-like masking for EU customers and mask emails/SSNs globally. I will attach our internal redaction policy (internal_policy_redaction.pdf) if helpful — I’ll share via the Drive link.

One more: is the recommended redwood-titan-7b-quant able to run in our Dedicated footprint (8x A100s) with the latency targets? We need a rough sizing estimate to confirm.

—Jane

Hi Jane —

Short answers: yes, titan-7b-quant can meet your latency targets in a Dedicated pool if we shard requests and enable prefix KV caching; I will include a sizing sketch below. We’ll also run a throughput simulation as part of the initial fit check.

Sizing sketch (8x A100s)
- Titan-7b-quant: expected steady-state QPS target 120–220 depending on batch/seq; 95th percentile latency under 150ms with continuous batching + prefix caching for 8–12 token KV hits.
- Fallback alpine-1.3b: serves spikes/bursts to hit p95 under 120ms for trimmed contexts.

QA/regression concerns and evaluation plan
- Baseline metrics: please include a snapshot of your current NDCG@10 and any human QA samples (even a small 500-row CSV helps).
- Evaluation we will run: per-model NDCG, rerank precision at k, hallucination rate, and safety redaction false negatives. We’ll produce a small eval report and flag any quality regressions relative to your baseline.

Prompt collection guidance (practical tips to fill the CSV)
- Column 1: prompt_text (literal user input) — do not include identifying tokens in this column unless you have explicit permission.
- Column 2: context_snippet (system context or prior query) — optional.
- Column 3: expected_outcome (short label: rerank/answer/filter) — helps us map models to use cases.
- Column 4: pii_flag (yes/no) and pii_type (email, ssn, phone, none).
- Column 5: notes (why this is an edge case).

If you prefer, we can accept a redacted set and a parallel mapping file that contains token indexes to be masked; otherwise provide a fully anonymized CSV.

Drive + secure upload
- Please upload to the Drive folder I created (link below) and set the folder access to "Redwood access only" or share via your SFTP.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmePromptCollectionSecure

I’ll coordinate with Karthik to run the fit check as soon as we have the files.

Thanks,
Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
